:::{#def-classification}
#### Classification

A **classification problem** is a statistical problem in which
we seek to assign each observation to one of two or more discrete categories
based on its observed features or predictors $x$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-class}
#### Class

The discrete categories of a classification problem (@def-classification)
are its **classes**.
Let $\scrC$ be a set of $K$ classes
(for example, $\scrC = \set{1, \dots, K}$,
or a set of text labels).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-classification-rule}
#### Classification rule

A **classification rule** $c$ maps features to classes
(@def-class):

$$c: x \mapsto c(x) \in \scrC$$ {#eq-classification}

:::
